# PROBE

> PROBE is a free username-intelligence tool that checks a public username across 322 functional sources and reports evidence-aware found, not-found, blocked, unknown, and manual-review results.

PROBE is intended for lawful research using publicly reachable information. A result is a lead, not proof of identity or ownership. Verify important findings independently.

## Primary pages

- [Username search](https://usernameprobe.com/): The interactive PROBE application and its current source coverage.
- [Audit Your Own Username Footprint in 15 Minutes](https://usernameprobe.com/blog/audit-your-username-footprint): Step-by-step self-audit of your own username footprint: listing handles, searching them, reviewing found accounts, reducing linking details, and retiring old accounts.
- [Choosing a Username That Doesn't Give You Away](https://usernameprobe.com/blog/choosing-a-private-username): Advice on choosing private usernames: avoiding personal details, using separate handles for separate contexts, checking a name before claiming it, and changing handles safely.
- [Honest by Default: Why PROBE Says Who It Is](https://usernameprobe.com/blog/honest-by-default): How PROBE identifies its requests, respects platform terms and rate limits, and why some technically checkable sources stay manual.
- [What We're Building Next](https://usernameprobe.com/blog/what-were-building-next): Blocker census of 80 manual or non-deciding sources, nightly canary checks, sources being verified for release, and planned infrastructure and measurement work.
- [How to Search a Username Across the Web](https://usernameprobe.com/blog/how-to-search-a-username): Practical guide to username searches: variants, reading found, not found, unknown, blocked and skipped results, verifying matches, and responsible use.
- [The internet isn't forever](https://usernameprobe.com/blog/the-internet-isnt-forever): Digital footprints fade, platforms shutter, and archives crumble. What link rot and ephemerality mean for username intelligence.
- [The soft 404 epidemic](https://usernameprobe.com/blog/the-soft-404-epidemic): Why modern single-page applications return HTTP 200 OK for every path, and how PROBE requires corroborating evidence before claiming a match.
- [Decay of the open web](https://usernameprobe.com/blog/decay-of-the-open-web): Over half of historical OSINT targets are defunct. Why catalog size is a vanity metric and ruthless source pruning protects scan integrity.
- [When a profile field stays empty](https://usernameprobe.com/blog/when-a-profile-field-stays-empty): Why unavailable metadata is not a missing account, a zero count, or proof of identity.
- [Reading an accuracy snapshot](https://usernameprobe.com/blog/reading-an-accuracy-snapshot): Saved 7 October campaign diagnostics: 772 checks across 265 automatic sources, 98.71% decision accuracy at 80.31% coverage, zero observed false positives, and only 129 calibration-eligible rows. Not a fresh campaign, definitive held-out estimate, or future-search guarantee.
- [Profile details pilot](https://usernameprobe.com/blog/profile-details-pilot): How PROBE shows public profile details (picture, name, bio) on found results, proving each value against two real accounts and a made-up control before showing it, without storing anything.
- [October 2026 accuracy update](https://usernameprobe.com/blog/checking-the-checks): How re-testing the evaluation labels raised decision accuracy to 98.69% and recall to 95.87% with zero observed false matches, separating real fixes from catalog changes.
- [What your username does not hide](https://usernameprobe.com/blog/what-your-username-doesnt-hide): Why behavior, metadata, and contextual pivots can connect accounts even when usernames are unique, and why those signals are not proof of identity.
- [September 2026 accuracy update](https://usernameprobe.com/blog/improving-accuracy-without-guessing): How PROBE improved decision accuracy, coverage, and recall while preserving zero observed false matches.
- [Methodology and accuracy](https://usernameprobe.com/blog/measuring-username-search-accuracy): How decision accuracy, coverage, uncertainty, and the 947-control evaluation are measured.
- [Why results can be unknown](https://usernameprobe.com/blog/why-probe-abstains): Why blocked or ambiguous responses are not forced into found or not-found classifications.
- [Maintaining 322 sources](https://usernameprobe.com/blog/maintaining-a-source-catalog): How the 272 automatic checks and 50 manual-only links are maintained.
- [Roadmap](https://usernameprobe.com/roadmap): Shipped capabilities and planned reliability work.
- [Privacy and acceptable use](https://usernameprobe.com/privacy): Data handling, local notes, submissions, and usage restrictions.
- [Blog index](https://usernameprobe.com/blog/): All published PROBE technical articles.

## Interpretation

- PROBE checks public web responses; it does not authenticate to third-party accounts.
- `found` means the source returned evidence consistent with a public profile.
- `not_found` means the source returned source-specific evidence that the profile is absent.
- `skipped` means a verified site-specific username rule rejected the input before any request; it is not a network-confirmed missing account. Sources without proven rules are still checked.
- Username preflight currently covers 33 catalog entries, including 22 single-subdomain lookups. Rules retain permissive legacy formats rather than copying stricter new-registration limits.
- `blocked` and `unknown` mean the available response was insufficient for a reliable decision.
- Ambiguous redirects, conflicting source evidence, and missing positive markers in incomplete responses abstain. Integrity abstentions cannot be promoted to current account matches using archived responses.
- Reviewed source adapters can use GET, HEAD or POST and explicit JSON evidence without changing the public profile link; adapter configuration is validated at startup.
- Manual-only links are useful investigation pivots but are not automatically classified.
- Current functional coverage is 322 sources: 272 automatic checks and 50 manual-only links.
- Result cards use colored status dots with accessible labels and hover descriptions; the scan totals and status filters retain their text labels.
- Site names sit beside their status dots. HTTP and abbreviated category badges share fixed dimensions; full category names remain available to assistive technology and on hover.
- Scan download, cancel and done controls use icons with accessible labels and hover descriptions. Download choices keep their format and result-scope labels.
- Static JavaScript delivery is limited to the required minified frontend bundles. Unminified scripts and source maps return 404; browser-delivered code remains publicly inspectable.
- Research tools stay collapsed before a scan and expand when scanning starts. They can be reopened or collapsed manually; this does not change which sources are checked.
- Manual pivots exclude duplicate general search engines and list TruePeopleSearch once for phone/name lookups. Only compatible targets are prefilled; unrelated scan inputs open the service homepage for manual entry.
- Research result panels scroll internally instead of stretching the reference links. The paper-colored navbar scrolls away with the page; scan progress stays at the viewport top.
- An outward-moving wave highlights the dotted background only during a scan. Motion preferences are respected throughout navigation and disclosures.

## Citation guidance

Cite the specific methodology or article page when discussing PROBE's measurements or decision rules. Include the measurement date when quoting accuracy figures because source behavior changes over time. Do not describe a username match as proof that two accounts belong to the same person.
